correctness.rationale: The four disjoint scalar/traceless strata give the exact integer Fourier formula (1) by orthogonality; a five-case table of hyperplane sections of a split three-space is verified by Witt coordinates. The q>=5 inequality excludes spurious 0/1/q-point intersections. The two-point condition yields exactly the nonzero-square discriminant, and counting isotropic and nonsquare vectors gives the nullity polynomial. The standalone checker from this same package exhaustively checks the symbolic formula and zero criterion at p=5,7, and direct Fourier coefficients at p=3 and selected p=5; q=3 is explicitly excluded. This is a proof for arbitrary odd prime powers, not an extrapolation. An independent exact GF(9) arithmetic checker uses the extension field F_3[u]/(u²+1) to compare 2850 frequencies with 152 observed zero-family hits.

value.rationale: The anticommuting (quantum-plane) matrix-pair variety is a canonical nonlinear finite-field algebraic object previously studied through geometry and point counts. Determining every Fourier-null frequency and the exact kernel of its natural additive convolution is a structural spectral invariant in an infinite family, with a surprising isotropic-versus-nonsquare obstruction and a genuine small-field boundary. It is not an arbitrary slice or routine substitution.
